clue.text: County men caught by other side include Yorkshire opener

indicators.note: the prisoners take the next letter into their midst, so include signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: soldiers captured by the enemy are POWs, prisoners of war

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, as an opening batsman goes in first

explanation.surface: A recruiting note about captured soldiers and a Yorkshire cricket opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yorkshire opener' sounds like a cricketer, but it simply gives Y, which goes inside POWS. POWYS is a county in mid-Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Powys is a large rural administrative area of Wales, one of its principal local-government divisions.

clue.text: Perfectly proficient?

parts.note: someone made perfect by repetition, since practice makes perfect

explanation.definitionFit: Being skilled through much rehearsal means being expert, the result that practice is said to make perfect.

clue.text: Quality a mariner discerned everywhere

definitions.meaning: the clarity or lustre of a diamond
Coleridge's Ancient Mariner sees it all round: 'everywhere, nor any drop to drink'

explanation.surface: A sailor saw quality wherever he looked.
explanation.walkthrough: In Coleridge's poem The Rime of the Ancient Mariner the becalmed sailor sees 'Water, water, everywhere'. The first sense is the grading of a gem's clarity.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds are graded by their transparency, called by this name, and the sea was all the becalmed seaman could see.

clue.text: Put in after firm's start to create easy job

indicators.note: put signals placing one piece into another
with firm's start, after tells where: the little word goes just behind the first letter

parts.note: firm means secure, steady

explanation.surface: An instruction to be inserted after a company's founding to make a cushy post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' suggests a company, but it means steady. 'Put ... after firm's start' says the short word goes just behind the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid position needing little or no work, so a cushy post.

clue.text: It helps racehorse to be first to jump

definitions.text: It helps racehorse to be first to jump

parts.words: It helps racehorse to be first to jump
parts.note: an early lead given before the off lets a runner reach the line first; read in pieces, being in front then leaping off the mark

explanation.surface: Advice on how a racehorse can get ahead at a jump.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads both as a description of an advantage and, in pieces, as 'be first' (HEAD) plus 'jump' (START).
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage granted at the outset of a race lets a runner lead from the beginning, which is what helps it win.

clue.text: Humble employee, initially -loathsome scamp, finally

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of each of the two words before it
finally picks out the closing letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A humble clerk who turns out, in the end, to be a loathsome rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep, the 'umble' clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield, is a loathsome scamp. 'initially' gives H, E; 'finally' gives E, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's fawning, scheming clerk in David Copperfield constantly proclaims himself 'umble' and proves a villain.

clue.text: Play strongly in favour of nothing

parts.note: to be all for something is to support it wholeheartedly
love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly backing something worth nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: All for Love is John Dryden's 1677 tragedy about Antony and Cleopatra.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryden's tragedy of Antony and Cleopatra is a drama for the stage.

clue.text: Dog, a matchless sort of boxer

definitions.meaning: to follow someone closely, as a verb
a fighter who spars alone with no opponent, so without a match

explanation.surface: A dog that is a boxer with no fights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' and 'boxer' make you think of the breed, but 'Dog' is the verb to follow and the boxer shadow-boxes against no opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone closely is to tail them like their own silhouette, and a fighter sparring against nobody practises with no rival.

clue.text: Successful candidate contrived 90% in paper, I note

annotationWithheld.why: Successful candidate contrived 90% in paper, I note (9): parse is an anagram of nine of the ten letters of PAPER I NOTE (R dropped, '90%' the deletion indicator), but the halvedAsDeletion rule reads any 'N%' indicator as a halving and refuses the deletion; a composite with bare R is refused too
annotationWithheld.clue: Successful candidate contrived 90% in paper, I note

clue.text: Alexander's beloved Asians

definitions.meaning: Thaïs, the Athenian courtesan who accompanied Alexander the Great

explanation.surface: Alexander the Great's affection for Asian peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: Thaïs was the Athenian courtesan said to have urged Alexander to burn Persepolis, celebrated in Dryden's Alexander's Feast.
explanation.definitionFit: The courtesan loved by Alexander shares her name with the nationals of Thailand, a south-east Asian country.

clue.text: So-called writer might alarm some Londoners

definitions.meaning: the pen-name under which Anne Brontë published her novels
a warning bell rung in Acton, a district of west London, would rouse its residents

explanation.surface: A pseudonymous author who could frighten Londoners.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne Brontë wrote as Acton Bell; Acton is a district of west London, so an alarm bell there might alarm some Londoners.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brontë sisters used male pseudonyms, Anne's being this one, so she was only so-called by it; a bell in that London district rings out alarms.

clue.text: Main star's central part in Greek drama

definitions.meaning: the brightest star in a constellation is designated by the first Greek letter
the Greek word drama is spelt delta-rho-...-mu-..., and its middle letter of the five is the first letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Praise for the leading actor at the heart of a Greek tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main star' suggests a leading actor, but it is the astronomical sense. The second reading needs the Greek spelling of drama: its third (central) letter is the Greek A.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers label the brightest star of each constellation with the first Greek letter, and that same letter sits in the middle of the Greek word for drama.

clue.text: Majority' of the people in the old country

indicators.note: most of the word, here all but its final letter, is kept

parts.note: a people or nation can be called a race

explanation.surface: A remark that most of the population lives in the old country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Majority of' keeps all but the last letter of the little word. Thrace was an ancient region of south-eastern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was an ancient land in the Balkans, inhabited by the Thracians and later divided among Greece, Bulgaria and Turkey.

clue.text: Part in Hamlet or Merchant of Venice back in America

parts.note: Marco Polo, the travelling merchant from Venice, not Shakespeare's play

indicators.note: the little word in is read backwards

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A question of whether a role belongs to Hamlet or The Merchant of Venice, now staged in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merchant of Venice' looks like the Shakespeare play beside Hamlet, but it is Marco POLO. 'back' turns IN into NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Polonius is the meddling counsellor, Ophelia's father, who is a role in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Liberal crossing the floor, as 27 might be

definitions.text: crossing the floor, as 27 might be
definitions.meaning: an Axminster carpet can be fitted to run across the whole floor from one side to the other

explanation.surface: A Liberal MP defecting to the other side of the House, like a carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' and 'crossing the floor' suggest a politician changing party in Parliament; instead they describe abundance and a fitted carpet. 27 is AXMINSTER, a kind of carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lavish and all-pervading covers everything, and fitted carpet runs from one side of the room to the other.

clue.text: Turnover from a couple of seasons, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, giving something that sounds like the answer

parts.note: one season of the year, summer, and a seasoning for food, salt

explanation.surface: A remark about sales turnover across two seasons of trading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' suggests business takings but means a head-over-heels roll. 'seasons' is used in two senses: a time of year and a seasoning; 'say' gives the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-over-heels flip turns the body right over, so it is a gymnastic turn.

clue.text: Ticket collectors' nemesis

parts.note: read not as a railway inspector but as the traffic warden whom motorists collecting parking tickets dread

explanation.definitionFit: A traffic warden patrolling parking bays hands out fines, the bane of drivers who collect them.

clue.text: Does have as partner such a speculator

definitions.meaning: does are female deer, whose mate is the male
on the Stock Exchange, someone who buys new shares hoping to sell them quickly at a profit

explanation.surface: A question of whether some investors have business partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the verb but is the plural of doe, female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer partners the doe, and the same name is London market slang for a quick-profit buyer of new issues.

clue.text: Unusual foresight, as exemplified by Pegasus

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters appear in an unaccustomed order

explanation.surface: Pegasus, the winged horse, showing unusual foresight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges FORESIGHT. Pegasus was a present to the hero Bellerophon from the goddess Athena.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena gave the winged steed to Bellerophon as a present, making it a horse received free.

clue.text: Latest play and novel

parts.note: Brand is a verse drama by Henrik Ibsen
novel as an adjective means new

explanation.surface: The newest play and novel on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' and 'novel' look like a pair of literary works, but 'novel' is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just made or bought is the most recent, the newest.

clue.text: At short notice, sent back information

indicators.note: both pieces together are read in reverse order

parts.note: a short form of advertisement, a notice, is ad

explanation.surface: Information returned at short notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns AT + AD, which gives DATA.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures, the raw material of knowledge.

clue.text: One of lucky foursome caught 50 on the other side

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
on the reverse of the page is overleaf

explanation.surface: A cricketer in a lucky team caught out for fifty on the far side of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture is a decoy: the lucky foursome is a four-leaf clover, and the answer is one of its leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-leafed clover is a traditional lucky charm, and each of its four parts is a leaf of that plant.

clue.text: Her intelligence provided James with title

definitions.text: Her intelligence provided James with title

parts.words: Her intelligence provided James with title
parts.note: the young girl whose knowledge gave Henry James the name of his novel What ___ Knew

explanation.surface: A female spy giving a man called James his title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intelligence' suggests spying; it means what the girl knew, from Henry James's 1897 novel What Maisie Knew.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James's novel What Maisie Knew is named for the knowledge of its child heroine.

clue.text: Jibes without difficulty as island appears

indicators.note: in the old sense outside: the jibes stand outside the next piece

parts.note: cutting remarks or jibes are barbs
ado is trouble or difficulty, as in without further ado

explanation.surface: Jibes are made easily as an island comes into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but here it has its old meaning 'outside', so the jibes go around the difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is a Caribbean nation lying in the Lesser Antilles.

clue.text: Advertisement for a jacket

parts.note: not a coat ad but the promotional text printed on a book's dust cover

explanation.definitionFit: Publishers print a short puff on a book's dust wrapper to sell it.

clue.text: Like Mercutio's scratch, no huge disaster

indicators.note: a disaster throws things into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mercutio's wound was a scratch, not a huge disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: In Romeo and Juliet the dying Mercutio calls his wound 'a scratch, a scratch... 'tis enough, 'twill serve'. 'disaster' rearranges NO HUGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercutio says of his fatal wound that it is sufficient, 'twill serve', so the scratch is described as sufficient.

clue.text: Like difficult radicals at heart

indicators.note: at heart means inside, so the letters are found running within the words

explanation.surface: Political radicals are difficult people at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' takes letters from inside 'difficult radicals'. The whole clue also describes extremists.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultras are extremists, so ultra means extreme, like hard-to-handle radicals.

clue.text: Northern (or Southern) sea-bird

parts.note: a mew is a gull, a sea-bird

explanation.surface: A bird of the northern seas, or perhaps the southern ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The smew is a small duck of northern waters; the bracketed '(or Southern)' supplies S to add to MEW, a gull.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small diving duck breeding in the far north and wintering on coasts and lakes.

clue.text: Our gunners left us outside range of Russians

indicators.note: the word us is placed around the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: British gunners left us outside a Russian firing range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like a firing range, but it is a mountain range. US goes 'outside' RA + L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Urals are the mountain chain in Russia that traditionally divides Europe from Asia.

clue.text: A church with cross in Devon town

indicators.note: the cross goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a minster is a large or important church
the letter X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: A church in a Devon town that has a cross in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Axminster is a town in Devon, England, famous for its carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a market town in east Devon, England.

clue.text: Member of temporary alliance given blanket coverage

definitions.text: Member of temporary alliance given blanket coverage

parts.words: Member of temporary alliance given blanket coverage
parts.note: a partner in a political pact, as in strange allies, read literally as someone sharing the covers

explanation.surface: A member of a short-term pact receives full media attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blanket coverage' suggests saturating press attention, but here it means lying under the same blankets.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sharing a bed is literally under the blankets with you, and figuratively an ally in an unlikely partnership.

clue.text: Soundly beat one in school

definitions.meaning: a member of a school, here a pod of marine mammals

explanation.surface: A teacher thrashing a pupil at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like a homophone signal, but 'soundly beat' is one sense: to thrash. A school is also a group of sea creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash someone hard is an old verb sense of the word, and the great sea mammal swims in a group called a school.
